user_direction: Rheinland ship in pirate service, rough repairs, unique forms using recesses; completely remove demonic character; explore round aft drum; do not use CORSAIR.

variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: carefully designed three-view game spaceship concept sheet for the user's Freelancer mod.

PRIMARY DIRECTION:
A RH / Rheinland Banshee fighter rebuilt and roughly maintained by pirates. It must FIRST read as an authentic RHEINLAND industrial ship, with pragmatic salvage repairs, uneven replacement sections, deliberate geometric volumes and cut-in mechanisms. The user completely rejected the previous demonic direction. Start fresh from the native references. No demons, horns, crowns, claws, predatory fins, skulls, black armour monster or Corsair design language. Do not use or echo the prior D01/D02 designs. Find a distinctive variation on the native fighter through its round aft mass, a newly sculpted neck and purposeful recesses. More inventive than tracing the stock mesh with fresh paint, but recognizably the same ship family.

REFERENCE ROLES:
1. Actual RH pirate FIGHTER in flight: source proportions, whole ship identity, low hanging cabin, elevated narrow circular rear mass, two short wings, ONE central rear engine.
2. IMMUTABLE fighter CABIN closeups: use this exact cabin, not any other cabin.
3. User-selected RH FREIGHTER Q13: ART DIRECTION and design-method reference only. Borrow its medium-scale detail density, deep inset panels, geometric depth changes at diagonal replacement joints, worn pale/red/olive salvage materials and restrained practical industrial mood. DO NOT copy this truck's hull, height, hump roof, cylinders, engine count, cabin or mechanisms.
4. Actual fighter BAYDOOR closed/open: top rectangular lid in the neck slides AFT and a little UP, into a pocket beneath the rear shoulder; no rotation.
5. Native wing phases: use the left column FLIGHT pose, wings swept FORWARD and slightly drooping DOWN/OUT. Each has inner sliding section + separately hinged outer section.

PROPORTIONS / UNCHANGED ANCHORS:
Compact narrow fighter, original flight size W10.9 H7.1 L13.6. Original cabin at the low front, original size and position. Short deep angled neck, high rear circular mass, a single rear axial engine. The ROUND aft drum is important: broad circular faces look PORT/STARBOARD, not forward; the cylinder axis goes across the ship. It is tall but transversely NARROW, a disk-like body rather than a sphere or wide barrel. Round in SIDE, narrow in TOP. Keep the outer circle strongly readable; give it a meaningful fresh three-dimensional construction specified below. Not an arbitrary faceted polygon hiding the circle. Aft drum is FIXED. One central exhaust out the rear, no wing engines or side thruster pods. New neck integrates with the drum as designed solid volumes, not a box bolted to a wheel.

CABIN EXACT:
Copy image 2: tall blunt faceted down-hanging cabin, sloped blue FRONT windshield and its lower blue band below the narrow yellow/black divider; tall trapezoid/triangular SIDE glass panes and broad original metal frames; small original overhanging brow; opaque stepped chin with red side inset, small lower blue corner slots, yellow/black bumper band and tapered underside. Do not add cabin armour or reshape glazing. No larger canopy, no freighter windows. The hull is newly designed BEHIND this unchanged module.

SUBTRACTIVE DESIGN / ROUGH REPAIR:
Form comes from sculpted major masses, deep pockets, recessed service fields, not an armour stack. Two or three large geometric recesses with visible solid floors and sidewalls: oblique stepped side bays, broad cut-in slots, circular or crescent recesses in the aft drum. Use lower continuous body edges, a restrained deliberate silhouette step, and functional depth transitions. These are true volume changes readable in plain clay, not only painted panel lines. Add several meaningful medium-scale access fields and deep inset vents with only a few broad vanes. Similar detail richness to Q13: neither a plain box nor thousands of greebles.
Pirate repairs appear in 2-3 physically fitted replacement regions whose diagonal seams do not quite align with the factory panel layout; a slightly different depth, material, size or cut corner; old paint fields interrupted by flush donor sections. Practical competent-enough field repairs, rough but functional. Predominantly integral flush or RECESSED parts. A few textured weld seams and scuffs, no surface bolt/rivet geometry. Rich worn pale warm-gray hull with muted red/olive/brown donor fields and understated dark recesses. No shiny factory symmetry of every cover, no uniform rusty ball. No national flags or crosses.
NO exposed pipes, hoses, cables or piston rods. NO exterior skeletal frames, trusses, braces, cages or floating rings. NO horns, spikes, giant overhanging armour shoulders or decorative projections. Recesses have solid backs. Keep angular authored corners, but clipped utilitarian wing ends, not giant knife wings. Main round forms stay circular.

FUNCTION:
Lid: a distinct RECTANGULAR recessed dorsal lid directly behind the cockpit. Show CLOSED. Leave a clear longitudinal rearward slide corridor and pocket; nothing fixed obstructs it. A small arrow beside it in TOP points aft labelled BAYDOOR. Rear drum does not rotate. This is not the freighter's curved rotating roof.
Wings: two short forward-swept wing assemblies beneath the neck. Roots seated in cut-in sliding sockets, modest meaningful solid hinge bearings at the inner-to-outer break, mostly nestled into the surfaces. Wing hinges rotate about fore-aft axes, not huge discs facing sideways. Outer wing stows UP ~63 degrees, inner carrier moves IN/UP/AFT; keep articulation breaks and clearance.
ALL views FLIGHT. TOP nose UP: left wing tip must lie UP-LEFT from root and right tip UP-RIGHT from root. Whole wing span reaches toward the NOSE, not tail. SIDE nose RIGHT: wing projects down and RIGHT from root. Maintain these projections. Do not turn the ship into a modern backward-swept jet. Similar original short span and chord, functional broad slightly clipped tips; no aggressive long blades.
Keep one axial rear engine, a compact closed collar, plausible unobstructed equipment mounting pads; no weapons used to fake ship complexity.

PAGE / STYLE:
ONE landscape concept sheet, exactly THREE consistent views of the SAME design: large 3/4 front-side on LEFT; true SIDE / FLIGHT upper RIGHT nose RIGHT; true TOP / FLIGHT lower RIGHT nose UP. Complete uncropped shapes, no extra inset. All views same cabin, drum construction, engine count, wings and closed hatch. Refined industrial marker/gouache concept painting, precise readable ink contours, good material separation, ivory paper. Borrow Q13's clarity and believable medium-scale depth, not its cargo-ship form. No cinematic darkness, environment, battle or background scene. Titles only as specified plus SIDE / FLIGHT and TOP / FLIGHT.

R01 SPECIFIC FORM — OFFSET CIRCULAR SEAT:
Reinterpret the original rear drum as one substantial clean ROUND closed housing with an inset circular side cover whose center is shifted a little FORWARD and DOWN within the outer circle. This creates a broad deep CRESCENT-SHAPED recessed service bay around the UPPER/AFT side of that inset cover. The crescent is cut INTO the side wall with a closed stepped floor and a few broad unequal service fields; it is not a separate floating hoop, open cage or turbine. The lower/front portion of the inner circular cover merges into a thick continuous angular neck saddle. Keep about 85% of the outer round silhouette unbroken. Give the outer curved barrel band 4-5 large inset repaired fields instead of raised ribs; one broad red donor sector interrupts the pale/olive factory band. A slight depth step and a wide slot across the curved band create real three-dimensional distinction in TOP and 3/4, without growing external fins.
Reshape the neck as a slightly descending solid spine with a compact stepped lower edge: one substantial elongated trapezoidal side recess has a diagonal replacement corner and a smaller inset grille behind it. The diagonal section change should give the side a fresh outline, not just repeat the source rectangular box. Keep the broad upper lid free. Wing root sits inside the lower neck recess. Short forward-swept wings are broad and utilitarian with one clipped tip corner, original overall span; a repaired outer section differs subtly from its inner section. Moderate asymmetric cover seams, balanced main structure. Restrained practical ship.
Title exactly: RH PIRATE FIGHTER / R01
